__**Concept:**__

**Infectious diseases:**

__
 
• The **disorders **or diseases caused by organisms such as **bacteria,** **viruses, fungi, or parasites **are called infectious diseases.
 
• Sometimes they are **harmless **but under certain conditions, some of these diseases can be proved **harmful **as well.

**Viral diseases:**

 
• Diseases caused by the different types of **viruses** are known as** viral diseases.**
 
• Some common types of viral diseases are** HIV, Ebola, Covid-19,** etc.

**Explanation:**__

**Hepatitis:**

__
 
• It is a condition when the human **liver is infected** by the **hepatitis virus.**
 
• It **disturbs the functions of the liver.**
 
• Such as the** production of bile, excretion, fat and protein metabolism, activation of enzymes, and synthesis of protein.**
 
• Can be diagnosed through a common blood test.
 
• There are some more kinds of hepatitis like hepatitis A, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, hepatitis D, and hepatitis E.

**Hepatitis B:**

 
• It is an infectious disease caused by the **hepatitis B virus.**
 
• This can be spread if a person gets in contact with **blood, saliva, or fluid of an infectious body.**
 
• Sharing the **personal belongings** of an infected person such as a **toothbrush or razor** can also cause hepatitis B.

**Symptoms:**

 
• Jaundice
 
• Feeling of tiredness
 
• Abdominal pain

**Thus, hepatitis is caused by a virus.**__

questions.question: Puccinia is a parasitic ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Fungus__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Puccinia**:-

 
 
• It is a **black stem rust of wheat and other cereals and grasses**.
 
• The scientific name is **Puccinia Graminis**.
 
• It is capable of producing infectious **urediniospores** as long as infected leaf tissue remains alive.
 
• Urediniospores can be **wind-disseminated **infect host plants hundreds of kilometers from their source plants.
 
 
 
• **Fungus**:-
 
 
• There are about** 144,00 known species of organisms of the kingdom fungi** including **yeasts, rusts, smuts, mildew, molds, and mushrooms**.
 
• Fungi are among the most widely distributed organisms on earth and are of **great environmental and medical importance**.
 
• Fungi are **eukaryotic organisms** which means their **cells contain membrane-bound organelles and clearly defined nuclei**.
 
• Together with bacteria, fungi are **responsible for breaking down organic matter and releasing carbon, oxygen, nitrogen and phosphorus into the soil and the atmosphere**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plant**:-

 
 
• Plant is any **multicellular eukaryotic life-form characterized by photosynthetic nutrition**.
 
• It plays a vital role in the **maintenance of life on earth**.
 
• All energy used by living organisms depends on the complex process of** photosynthesis which is mostly carried out by green plants**.
 
 
 
• **Algae**:-
 
 
• Algae are **chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, and largely aquatic(both freshwater and marine ) organisms**.
 
• They occur in a variety of other habitats: moist stones, soils, and wood.
 
 
 
• **Animal**:-
 
 
• It is a **group of multicellular eukaryotic organisms**.
 
• They are thought to have **evolved independently from the unicellular eukaryotes**.
 
• Animals **dominate human conceptions of life on Earth** not simply by their size, abundance, and sheer diversity but also by their mobility, a trait that humans share.

__
 
• **Zinc **helps to produce the active form of vitamin A and transports it across the body.
 
• Zinc is an important mineral involved in various bodily functions – **growth and development as well as immune function**.

• red meat
 
• shellfish
 
• poultry
 
• milk and cheese
 
• whole grains cereals with added zinc

questions.question: Name the disorder tied to body image distortion in adolescence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** anorexia nervosa.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Anorexia nervosa is a serious eating disorder that is characterized by body image distortion, an intense fear of gaining weight, and restriction of food intake.**
 
• It commonly affects adolescents, especially females, and can lead to severe physical and psychological consequences if left untreated.
 
• Schizophrenia is a mental disorder that affects a person's ability to think, feel, and behave clearly, causing hallucinations, delusions, and disordered thinking.
 
• Depression is a mood disorder that causes persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest, and can affect a person's ability to function in daily life.
 
• Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disorder that affects memory, thinking, and behavior, and is more commonly associated with elderly individuals.

questions.question: To which phylum do round worms belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Aschelminthes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Roundworms** belong to the phylum Aschelminthes**
 
• Aschelminthes:
 
 
• The Aschelminthes, closely associated with the Platyhelminthes, is an obsolete phylum of pseudocoelomate.
 
• Other similar animals that are no longer considered closely related and have been promoted to phyla in their own right.
 
• Previously, phylum Aschelminthes included seven diverse classes of animals - Nematoda (or Nemata), Rotifera, Acanthocephala, Gastrotricha, Kinorhyncha (or Echinodera), Nematomorpha, and Gnathostomulida.
 
• The Aschelminthes are commonly called roundworms because the body appears circular in the transverse cross-section.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Annelida**:

 
 
• Phylum Annelida includes **segmented worms, such as earthworms and leeche**s.
 
• These organisms are characterized by their segmented bodies and well-developed coelom (body cavity).
 
 
 
• **Ctenophora**:
 
 
• Phylum Ctenophora includes **comb jellies, which are marine invertebrates** known for their ciliated bands used for movement.
 
• They are radially symmetrical and lack stinging cells (like those found in jellyfish).
 
 
 
• **Platyhelminthes**:
 
 
• Phylum Platyhelminthes includes **flatworms, such as tapeworms and planarians.**
 
• These organisms are characterized by their flat, unsegmented bodies and lack of a body cavity (acoelomates).
